Job T08: usp_fraud_flags (tsql), file estate/tsql/T08_usp_fraud_flags.sql.
Rule-based fraud indicators for recently notified claims.

Code:
  1 | /*==============================================================================
  2 |   Job       rpt.usp_fraud_flags
  3 |   Purpose   Fraud indicators for the Special Investigations Unit (SIU): one row
  4 |             per claim notified in the twelve months to the reporting date, with
  5 |             the indicator flags, a score and a referral band for the SIU
  6 |             worklist and case tool.
  7 |   Author    MOB
  8 |   Run by    SIU_WEEKLY, after the claims and policy extracts and dw.dim_customer
  9 |             have loaded
 10 |   Output    rpt.claim_fraud_flags (full refresh)
 11 | 
 12 |   Change log
 13 |     2016-05-09  MOB   Initial version: early notification and new customer
 14 |                       indicators (CR-0954)
 15 |     2016-11-21  MOB   Motor claims: registration not in the Irish format
 16 |                       (CR-1012)
 17 |     2017-04-03  SB    Claim keyed against a policy from another line of
 18 |                       business (INC-1530)
 19 |     2018-08-27  SB    fraud_score and referral bands agreed with SIU (CR-1377)
 20 |     2019-02-11  NF    Policy dates from the latest policy extract on or before
 21 |                       the reporting date, not the old policy master (CR-1529)
 22 |     2020-06-15  NF    loss_day_key and reason text for the SIU case tool
 23 |                       (CR-1810)
 24 |     2021-10-04  SB    lob_code upper-cased for the SIU dashboard (INC-2389)
 25 | ==============================================================================*/
 26 | SET NOCOUNT ON;
 27 | GO
 28 | IF OBJECT_ID(N'rpt.claim_fraud_flags', N'U') IS NULL
 29 | CREATE TABLE rpt.claim_fraud_flags (
 30 |     claim_id                 INT            NOT NULL,
 31 |     claim_number             VARCHAR(20)    NOT NULL,
 32 |     policy_id                INT            NOT NULL,
 33 |     policy_number            VARCHAR(20)    NULL,
 34 |     customer_id              INT            NOT NULL,
 35 |     lob_code                 VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
 36 |     loss_date                DATE           NOT NULL,
 37 |     reported_date            DATE           NOT NULL,
 38 |     early_notification_flag  INT            NOT NULL,
 39 |     invalid_reg_flag         INT            NOT NULL,
 40 |     new_customer_flag        INT            NOT NULL,
 41 |     lob_mismatch_flag        INT            NOT NULL,
 42 |     fraud_score              INT            NOT NULL,
 43 |     fraud_band               VARCHAR(6)     NOT NULL,  -- HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW
 44 |     loss_day_key             CHAR(8)        NOT NULL,  -- yyyymmdd, day key in the case tool
 45 |     reason_text              VARCHAR(100)   NOT NULL,
 46 |     as_of_date               DATE           NOT NULL,
 47 |     CONSTRAINT pk_rpt_claim_fraud_flags PRIMARY KEY (claim_id)
 48 | );
 49 | GO
 50 | CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE rpt.usp_fraud_flags
 51 |     @AsOfDate DATE
 52 | AS
 53 | BEGIN
 54 |     SET NOCOUNT ON;
 55 | 
 56 |     DECLARE @job_name       VARCHAR(128) = 'rpt.usp_fraud_flags',
 57 |             @rows           INT,
 58 |             @snapshot_date  DATE,
 59 |             @err_msg        NVARCHAR(4000),
 60 |             @err_no         INT;
 61 | 
 62 |     BEGIN TRY
 63 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';
 64 | 
 65 |         /* Policy details from the latest policy extract on or before the reporting date */
 66 |         SELECT  @snapshot_date = MAX(ps.snapshot_date)
 67 |         FROM    stg.policy_snapshots ps WITH (NOLOCK)
 68 |         WHERE   ps.snapshot_date <= @AsOfDate;
 69 | 
 70 |         /* 1. Claims notified in the twelve months to the reporting date, with the
 71 |               policy they were made under and when the policyholder became a customer */
 72 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#claims') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #claims;
 73 | 
 74 |         SELECT  c.claim_id,
 75 |                 c.claim_number,
 76 |                 c.policy_id,
 77 |                 c.customer_id,
 78 |                 c.lob_code,
 79 |                 c.loss_date,
 80 |                 c.reported_date,
 81 |                 p.policy_number,
 82 |                 p.inception_date,
 83 |                 p.expiry_date,
 84 |                 p.vehicle_reg,
 85 |                 dc.customer_since
 86 |         INTO    #claims
 87 |         FROM    stg.claims c WITH (NOLOCK)
 88 |         LEFT JOIN stg.policy_snapshots p WITH (NOLOCK)
 89 |                ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id
 90 |               AND p.snapshot_date = @snapshot_date
 91 |         LEFT JOIN dw.dim_customer dc WITH (NOLOCK)
 92 |                ON dc.customer_id = c.customer_id
 93 |         WHERE   c.reported_date >  DATEADD(MONTH, -12, @AsOfDate)
 94 |           AND   c.reported_date <= @AsOfDate;
 95 | 
 96 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
 97 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'claims notified', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
 98 | 
 99 |         /* 2. SIU indicators, one point each (CR-0954, CR-1012, INC-1530) */
100 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#flags') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #flags;
101 | 
102 |         SELECT  f.*,
103 |                 f.early_notification_flag + f.invalid_reg_flag
104 |                   + f.new_customer_flag + f.lob_mismatch_flag     AS fraud_score
105 |         INTO    #flags
106 |         FROM   (SELECT  cl.claim_id,
107 |                         -- claim notified within 30 days of the cover starting
108 |                         CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(DAY, cl.expiry_date, cl.reported_date) BETWEEN 0 AND 30
109 |                              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS early_notification_flag,
110 |                         -- motor: registration not in the Irish format, e.g. 191-D-12345
111 |                         CASE WHEN cl.lob_code = 'MOT'
112 |                               AND cl.vehicle_reg NOT LIKE '[0-9][0-9]%-[A-Z]%-[0-9]%'
113 |                              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS invalid_reg_flag,
114 |                         -- customer for less than six months at the date of loss
115 |                         CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(DAY, cl.customer_since, cl.loss_date) < 180
116 |                              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS new_customer_flag,
117 |                         -- policy number starts with its line of business (MOT/2024/500001)
118 |                         CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(cl.policy_number, 0, 4) <> cl.lob_code
119 |                              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS lob_mismatch_flag
120 |                 FROM    #claims cl) f;
121 | 
122 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
123 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'indicators', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
124 | 
125 |         /* 3. Reload the SIU table: bands agreed with SIU (CR-1377) */
126 |         BEGIN TRANSACTION;
127 | 
128 |         TRUNCATE TABLE rpt.claim_fraud_flags;
129 | 
130 |         INSERT INTO rpt.claim_fraud_flags
131 |                (claim_id, claim_number, policy_id, policy_number, customer_id, lob_code,
132 |                 loss_date, reported_date, early_notification_flag, invalid_reg_flag,
133 |                 new_customer_flag, lob_mismatch_flag, fraud_score, fraud_band,
134 |                 loss_day_key, reason_text, as_of_date)
135 |         SELECT  cl.claim_id,
136 |                 cl.claim_number,
137 |                 cl.policy_id,
138 |                 cl.policy_number,
139 |                 cl.customer_id,
140 |                 UPPER(RTRIM(cl.lob_code)),
141 |                 cl.loss_date,
142 |                 cl.reported_date,
143 |                 f.early_notification_flag,
144 |                 f.invalid_reg_flag,
145 |                 f.new_customer_flag,
146 |                 f.lob_mismatch_flag,
147 |                 f.fraud_score,
148 |                 CASE WHEN f.fraud_score >= 2 THEN 'HIGH'
149 |                      WHEN f.fraud_score = 1  THEN 'MEDIUM'
150 |                      ELSE 'LOW'
151 |                 END,
152 |                 CONVERT(CHAR(8), cl.loss_date, 112),
153 |                 'Notified ' + CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), cl.reported_date, 103)
154 |                     + CASE WHEN f.fraud_score = 0 THEN ' - no indicators' ELSE ' -' END
155 |                     + CASE WHEN f.early_notification_flag = 1 THEN ' EARLY'   ELSE '' END
156 |                     + CASE WHEN f.invalid_reg_flag        = 1 THEN ' REG'     ELSE '' END
157 |                     + CASE WHEN f.new_customer_flag       = 1 THEN ' NEWCUST' ELSE '' END
158 |                     + CASE WHEN f.lob_mismatch_flag       = 1 THEN ' LOB'     ELSE '' END,
159 |                 @AsOfDate
160 |         FROM    #claims cl
161 |         JOIN    #flags f
162 |                 ON f.claim_id = cl.claim_id;
163 | 
164 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
165 | 
166 |         COMMIT TRANSACTION;
167 | 
168 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'rpt.claim_fraud_flags', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
169 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
170 |     END TRY
171 |     BEGIN CATCH
172 |         IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
173 | 
174 |         SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
175 |                 @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();
176 | 
177 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
178 |              @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
179 |         THROW;
180 |     END CATCH
181 | END;
182 | GO

Trap cards:
- TSQL-01 (semantic) Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins. Legacy: Under a case-insensitive collation such as SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text compares equal regardless of letter case (and of trailing spaces, see TSQL-02): state = 'ACTIVE' also matches 'Active' and 'active'; GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and join keys put case variants together. The stored value is returned unchanged. Spark: Spark compares strings in binary order: 'Active' <> 'ACTIVE', so a filter drops case variants, a GROUP BY splits them into separate groups and a join misses them.
- TSQL-02 (semantic) Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces. Legacy: SQL Server pads the shorter string with spaces before comparing, so 'WEST ' = 'WEST' (also in IN, GROUP BY and joins). CHAR(n) and NCHAR(n) values are stored and returned padded to n characters: 'AB' in a CHAR(4) column is 'AB '. LEN() ignores trailing spaces (TSQL-15). Leading spaces always count. Spark: Spark compares strings exactly, so 'WEST ' <> 'WEST', and its string type never pads. A value read from a CHAR source column keeps whatever spaces it was stored with.
- TSQL-03 (semantic) Integer division truncates. Legacy: INT / INT is integer division in T-SQL, truncating toward zero: 7 / 2 = 3, -7 / 2 = -3. The result type follows the operands, so the fraction is lost before any later cast, e.g. CAST(qty / pack_size AS DECIMAL(9,2)) or 100 * a / b. Spark: Spark's / always returns a double (7 / 2 = 3.5); DIV is integer division.
- TSQL-04 (semantic) DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed, not elapsed periods. Legacy: DATEDIFF(datepart, a, b) counts the datepart boundaries crossed between a and b: DATEDIFF(year, '2025-12-31', '2026-01-01') = 1 and DATEDIFF(month, '2025-01-31', '2025-02-01') = 1. DATEDIFF(week, ...) counts Sundays crossed, whatever SET DATEFIRST says. DATEDIFF(day, ...) on DATE values equals the day difference. Spark: datediff(end, start) counts days (arguments reversed); months_between returns a fraction with its own month-end rule; floor(months/12) counts elapsed years, not boundaries.
- TSQL-05 (semantic) + concatenation with NULL yields NULL. Legacy: With CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL ON (the default), 'A' + NULL is NULL, so a whole concatenation is NULL when any part is. CONCAT() and CONCAT_WS() treat NULL as empty. Spark: Spark's + is arithmetic only; concat() returns NULL when any argument is NULL, while concat_ws() skips NULLs and format_string writes 'null'.
- TSQL-06 (semantic) ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks. Legacy: ISNULL(a, b) returns a's data type, so the replacement b is converted to it: a VARCHAR(5) column with ISNULL(col, 'UNKNOWN') returns 'UNKNO' (truncated), and ISNULL(int_col, 0.5) returns 0. COALESCE uses the highest-precedence type instead. Change detection written as ISNULL(src, '') <> ISNULL(tgt, '') treats NULL and '' as the same value. Spark: coalesce() keeps the replacement as written ('UNKNOWN') and widens types; it never truncates.
- TSQL-07 (semantic) DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values. Legacy: DECIMAL arithmetic follows fixed precision and scale rules (e.g. division keeps at least 6 decimal places, results are capped at 38 digits and the scale shrinks to fit); intermediate results are rounded at each step to their result type. ROUND(x, n) rounds half away from zero; ROUND(x, n, 1) truncates. Assigning to a DECIMAL(p,s) column rounds. Spark: Spark's decimal rules are similar but not identical (scale reduction, and doubles if an operand is a double literal); F.round on a double rounds the binary value, so a computed 2.675 (really 2.67499...) rounds to 2.67; bround is half-even.
- TSQL-08 (semantic) TOP and TOP WITH TIES. Legacy: TOP n returns n rows in ORDER BY order (arbitrary among ties unless the ORDER BY is unique); TOP n WITH TIES also returns every row tied with the last one. Spark: limit(n) after orderBy returns exactly n rows; ties need a rank window.
- TSQL-09 (construct) CROSS APPLY / OUTER APPLY with TOP 1. Legacy: CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 ... WHERE inner.k = outer.k ORDER BY ...) picks one inner row per outer row and drops outer rows with no match; OUTER APPLY keeps them with NULLs. Spark: Spark has no APPLY; a lateral subquery or a window replaces it.
- TSQL-10 (construct) UPDATE ... FROM. Legacy: UPDATE t SET ... FROM t JOIN s ON ... updates each target row from one matching source row; with several matches, which one wins is undefined. Spark: DataFrames are immutable; an update becomes a join plus a select.
- TSQL-11 (construct) MERGE and type-2 history. Legacy: MERGE matches target and source rows and updates, inserts or deletes in one statement. Type-2 history closes the current version (valid_to, is_current) of changed rows and inserts a new current version; IDENTITY keys are assigned in the INSERT's ORDER BY order, continuing from the table's highest value. Spark: Spark has no MERGE on DataFrames (Delta MERGE exists for tables); the job must compute the new state as a whole table from the previous state and the batch.
- TSQL-12 (construct) Cursors and WHILE loops. Legacy: A cursor processes rows one at a time in its ORDER BY order; variables carry state between rows (running totals, last values). NULL arithmetic inside the loop propagates: SET @total = @total + NULL makes @total NULL for the rest of the loop. Spark: Spark is set-based; loops become aggregations or ordered windows.
- TSQL-13 (construct) Temp tables. Legacy: #temp tables hold intermediate results for the session. Spark: Intermediate results are DataFrames or temporary views.
- TSQL-14 (semantic) LIKE character classes. Legacy: T-SQL LIKE supports character classes: '[0-9]' matches one digit, '[A-Z]' one letter (case-insensitively under a CI collation), '[^0-9]' a non-digit; % and _ as usual. Spark: Spark's LIKE has only % and _; '[0-9]' matches the literal text '[0-9]'.
- TSQL-15 (semantic) LEN ignores trailing spaces; SUBSTRING from 0; LEFT and RIGHT. Legacy: LEN(x) does not count trailing spaces (DATALENGTH does). SUBSTRING(x, 0, n) returns n-1 characters, because position 0 is before the string. LEFT/RIGHT count characters. Spark: length() counts trailing spaces; substring(x, 0, n) is treated like position 1 and returns n characters.
- TSQL-16 (semantic) CONVERT style codes. Legacy: CONVERT(type, date, style) formats dates by style: 101 mm/dd/yyyy, 103 dd/mm/yyyy, 104 dd.mm.yyyy, 105 dd-mm-yyyy, 106 dd mon yyyy, 111 yyyy/mm/dd, 112 yyyymmdd, 120 yyyy-mm-dd hh:mi:ss, 121 with milliseconds, 23 yyyy-mm-dd. Converting into a shorter CHAR(n)/VARCHAR(n) silently keeps the first n characters: CONVERT(CHAR(6), d, 112) is yyyymm. Spark: A cast to string gives yyyy-MM-dd; date_format needs a Java pattern; nothing truncates.
- TSQL-17 (construct) PIVOT. Legacy: PIVOT (aggregate(value) FOR col IN ([a], [b])) groups by every other column of the source and turns listed values into columns; values not listed are dropped; missing combinations give NULL. Spark: groupBy(...).pivot(col, values).agg(...) does the same when the values are listed; the grouping columns must be stated explicitly.
- TSQL-18 (semantic) EOMONTH and DATEADD at month-end. Legacy: DATEADD(month, n, d) clamps to the last day of the target month: DATEADD(month, 1, '2024-01-31') = '2024-02-29'; adding months to an earlier date never moves to a month-end. EOMONTH(d, n) returns the last day of the month n months away. Spark: add_months clamps the same way but also moves a last-day-of-month input to the target month's last day (add_months('2024-02-29', 1) = '2024-03-31'); last_day(d) is EOMONTH.
- TSQL-19 (semantic) Text ordering under collations (accents, case) in ORDER BY, MIN, MAX and rankings. Legacy: Under SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text sorts case-insensitively with accent rules (Á sorts with A); MIN/MAX on text and ORDER BY text in a ranking follow that order. Spark: Spark sorts strings by code point: 'Zoe' < 'aoife' and 'Á' sorts after 'Z'.

findings.note: DATEADD(MONTH,-12,@AsOfDate) only clamps to a month-end when it has to. Spark add_months also moves a month-end input to a month-end, so @AsOfDate = 2025-02-28 gives 2024-02-29 instead of 2024-02-28 and the 12-month window changes. Latent: only month-end reporting dates trigger it.

lob_code is VARCHAR(5). Under the CI collation, 'mot' and 'Mot' match 'MOT', so those claims get the motor registration check; a plain Spark equality would skip them. The later UPPER() suggests mixed-case values really exist.
lob_code is VARCHAR(5), and the RTRIM at line 140 shows it can carry trailing spaces. 'MOT ' = 'MOT' in SQL Server but not in Spark.

The LIKE pattern uses the [0-9] and [A-Z] character classes, and [A-Z] is case-insensitive under the CI collation. Spark LIKE would read them as literal text, so it must become an rlike with case-insensitive letters.
SUBSTRING(policy_number, 0, 4) returns only 3 characters in T-SQL. Spark substring(x, 0, 4) returns 4, which would change every lob_mismatch_flag.
The <> compares text with text: a substring of policy_number (VARCHAR) against lob_code (VARCHAR). Under the CI collation, a case difference such as 'mot' vs 'MOT' is not a mismatch; in Spark it is.
SQL Server ignores trailing spaces when comparing, so a lob_code of 'MOT ' equals the 3-character prefix 'MOT'. Spark would raise the mismatch flag.
CONVERT style 112 gives yyyymmdd and needs date_format 'yyyyMMdd'. A plain cast would give yyyy-MM-dd, which also breaks the CHAR(8) key.
CONVERT style 103 gives dd/mm/yyyy in the reason text and needs date_format 'dd/MM/yyyy'. A string cast would give yyyy-MM-dd.
The #claims temp table holds the claims enriched with policy and customer data; in Spark it becomes a DataFrame.
The #flags temp table holds the indicator flags and score; in Spark it becomes a DataFrame.
